# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-3 (Extended v62)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—evening/night of Valjean's theft and flight; Battle of Waterloo/Hougomont siege, June 17-18; June 18-19 evening/night post-battle looting); 1817 (carrier sighting; young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil cook-shop, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral appointment and town transformation); **1823 January (Fantine's arrest and street incident; Javert's revelation; Valjean's acute crisis; TRIAL SEQUENCE: Journey to Arras through February, arriving evening near eight o'clock; TRIAL EVENING SESSION; witnesses testify; Valjean reveals himself; acquittal of Champmathieu; arrest order issued; RETURN TO M. SUR M. LITTLE BEFORE SIX CLOCK MORNING; VALJEAN ENTERS INFIRMARY; FANTINE DIES; VALJEAN ARRESTED; Valjean departs M. sur M. marching toward Paris carrying bundle, dressed in workman's blouse)**; **1815 June 18-19 (midnight onward: post-Waterloo looting; mysterious prowler in blouse on hollow road of Ohain; sutler's wagon hidden behind hovel at Mont-Saint-Jean to Braine-l'Alleud road angle; woman seated in wagon among coffers and packages)**; **autumn of first year / 1815 onward (trial aftermath reflected; current narrative time at Dunstead harbor town)**; October 1823 (ship Orion enters Toulon port after heavy weather, for repairs); **November 17, 1823 (convict Jean Valjean fell from rigging into sea between Orion and frigate Algésiras, drowned, body not found, presumed entangled in Arsenal piles; newspaper account published)**; **Christmas Eve 1823 (Montfermeil tavern scene, men drinking and smoking, discussion of wine/grapes, mill operation)**; 1827 February (M. de Villèle parliamentary remarks on tax collection); 1849 (chapel walls freshly whitewashed); 1861/1862 (narrative reflection, traveller departing from Nivelles toward La Hulpe)
- Primary locations: M. sur M.; Montfermeil (between Livry and Chelles, southern edge of lofty plateau separating Ourcq from Marne; in 1823 a village in forest with pleasure-houses, church, spring near road to Chelles, ponds toward Gagny, water-carrier earning eight sous daily); Arras; Nivelles; La Hulpe; Braine-l'Alleud; Lillois; Genappe; Hal; Tongres; Hougomont; Mont-Saint-Jean plateau; Belle-Alliance; Abbey of Villiers forest; Rossomme farm; village of Ohain; hollow road of Ohain; Chapelle-Saint-Lambert; Wavre; Dion-le-Mont; Plancenoit; forest of Paris; Papelotte; Frischemont; Boitsfort; Groenendael; Soignes forest; Waterloo battlefield; **Dunstead (harbor town); Toulon port (dry dock, Arsenal quay, Arsenal point piles); Brest; Gagny; Chelles; Livry**; England (Hampstead, Hull, Liverpool, Dunstead/Kelford, Suffolk, London, Welbeck Street, Lowestoft, Torton, Kelmere, Dunby, Yarlby, Ostcombe, Ravenmere); Mediterranean; Balearic Isles; Nanterre; Suresnes; Breton wheat regions

## Waterloo Battle and Post-Battle Looting
[As previously recorded: sixty thousand killed; mysterious looting and prowler; hidden sutler's wagon; hollow road conditions; cuirassier officer rescue; philosophical debate on plunder; Restoration masquerade follows]

## Post-Waterloo and Restoration Era (1815-1823)
[As previously recorded: Napoleon's lingering influence; new France seeking Liberty; Congress of Vienna; Napoleon captive at Saint Helena; 1823 Spanish campaign critique; 1830 consequence germinated in 1823]

## Valjean Trial, Arrest, and Death (1823)
- **Trial sequence (January 1823)**: Valjean revealed himself at Arras trial; Champmathieu acquitted; arrest order issued; Valjean returned to M. sur M. little before six o'clock morning; Valjean entered infirmary; Fantine died; Valjean arrested
- **Imprisonment and Toulon assignment**: Valjean departed M. sur M. under arrest; imprisoned at Toulon; assigned to convict detachment aboard ship Orion
- **Death (November 17, 1823)**: While returning from rescue of sailor, Valjean fell from rigging into sea between Orion and frigate Algésiras anchored alongside; body not recovered, presumed entangled in Arsenal point piles; newspaper recorded him under number 9,430; official name: Jean Valjean; death presumed drowned

## The Orion Incident: Rescue at Toulon (October 1823)
**Ship's Condition**: Orion entered Toulon port after heavy weather for repairs; long ailing, barnacles on keel; prior dry dock cleaning damaged keel bolts; near Balearic Isles, sides strained and opened, ship sprung leak; equinoctial gale staved in grating/porthole on larboard side, damaged foretop-gallant-shrouds; later employed at Brest as school-ship, Mediterranean squadron

**Topman's Fall and Rescue (October 1823)**: Crew bending sails; topman lost balance taking upper corner of main-topsail on starboard; fell, seized footrope with both hands, remained hanging; violent swinging motion like stone in sling; most sailors (recently levied fishermen) dared not attempt rescue; topman losing strength, arms contracted in horrible twitchings; did not shout to conserve strength

**Convict Rescuer (Valjean)**: Man in red (convict from galley detachment) with green cap; asked permission to risk life saving topman; **broke chain riveted to ankle with one blow of hammer** (FACT: ease of chain-breaking noted only later, suspicious); climbed with tiger-cat agility; reached top, gust carried away cap revealing perfectly white head—not young man; fastened rope to yard point; descended hand over hand, creating second suspended figure; secured topman with cord; climbed back on yard, dragged sailor up; held him to recover strength; grasped him in arms, carried him on yard to cap, then to main-top; left him in comrades' hands

**Fall and Death**: Valjean began descent to rejoin detachment; dropped into rigging, ran along lower yard; at certain moment appeared to hesitate and stagger; fell into sea; perilous fall between Orion and frigate Algésiras; did not rise to surface; disappeared without ripple "as though fallen into cask of oil"; four men launched boat; search continued until evening; body never found

**Metaphorical Significance**: Spider bringing life not death; moment of immense force culminating in immense feebleness affords men food for thought

## Montfermeil/Dunstead Community: Ongoing Daily Life and Mysteries

**Dunstead Community Daily Actions and Relationships (Autumn, contemporary narrative)**:
- **Pewyn**: counted coins twice, penny short; gave Nylia Corrford solemn promise to rebuild fallen wall at Quenford (COMMITMENT)
- **Yewyn Corrford** (also called Yewyn Haskick): appeared tired; bought ribbon, regretted it; asked Lura if it will rain; agreed with Kassa about salt price scandal
- **Ulrald Corrford**: complained of aching back; gave Lura Haskick solemn promise to pay old debt owed to Stenson family (COMMITMENT); counted coins twice, penny short
- **Nylia Corrford**: complained of aching back; gave Pewyn solemn promise to rebuild fallen wall at Quenford (COMMITMENT); read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half the saints
- **Yera Haskick**: gave Yewyn Corrford solemn promise to carry sealed letter to Dungate (COMMITMENT); late one night confided to Kassa Brackick that Stenenridge mill ledger was rewritten after the flood (CLAIM)
- **Lura Haskick**: recipient of Ulrald's debt-payment promise; mended torn sleeve by window, said little; shrugged when asked about rain
- **Kassa Brackick**: told Yewyn "price of salt is scandal"; received Yera's confidence about mill ledger
- **Elra Corrford**: spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight; watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly; walked long way round to avoid muddy square; told Marald he looked tired
- **Marald Corrford**: asked about rain; confirmed looking tired
- **Rozek Stenenridge**: burned letter after reading; found work in Staveford, moved there, did not return; **CLAIM**: Luena followed him to Staveford within the month
- **Fenelle**: read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half the saints
- **Environmental backdrop**: Ruts and puddles after thaw; crooked sun chalked on forge wall; smoke from chimneys lay flat over fields; baker's boy late, line at oven grew long; frost silvered hedges overnight; bell for vespers rang thinly; children chased hoop shrieking; cart with turnips creaked past well; dog barked at nothing; wind off water smelled of salt and tar; bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage; gulls quarreled over fish heads by steps; rain threatened since morning but held off

## Montfermeil Village Description (1823)
- Located between Livry and Chelles on southern edge of plateau separating Ourcq from Marne
- In 1823: small village in forest, not large town; pleasure-houses of last century present with grand air, twisted iron balconies, long windows with tiny panes casting green shades on white shutters
- Peaceful, charming place not on road to anywhere; peasants lived cheaply and easily
- Water rare due to plateau elevation: end toward Gagny drew from magnificent forest ponds; other end (toward church and Chelles) found water only at spring half-way down slope near road to Chelles, quarter hour walk from village
- Households had difficulty keeping supplied; large houses (aristocracy including Thénardier tavern) paid half farthing per bucketful to water-carrier earning about eight sous daily; carrier worked until seven o'clock summer, five o'clock winter; after shutters closed, those without water either fetched themselves or went without

## Cosette's Condition and Labor (Christmas Eve 1823)
- Useful to Thénardiers in two ways: mother paid them; child served them
- When mother ceased paying (Fantine's circumstances), Thénardiers kept Cosette as servant
- Child greatly terrified of going to spring at night; took great care water never lacking in house
- On Christmas Eve: in usual place on cross-bar of kitchen table near chimney; wore rags; bare feet thrust in wooden shoes; by firelight knitting woollen stockings for young Thénardiers; very young kitten playing among chairs

## Thénardier Tavern Scene (Christmas Eve 1823)
- Number of men (carters, peddlers) seated drinking and smoking around four or five candles in public room
- Room resembled all drinking-shops: tables, pewter jugs, bottles, drinkers, smokers; little light, great noise
- 1823 fashionable bourgeois objects present: kaleidoscope and lamp of ribbed tin
- Female Thénardier attending to supper roasting before clear fire; husband drinking with customers, talking politics
- Discussion of vines near Nanterre and Suresnes flourishing; grapes, juice, wine quality; Breton wheat grinding problems (contains tares, fennel, vetches, hempseed, fox-tail, pebbles); miller complains people blame flour when it's grain fault
- Éponine and Azelma's laughter and chatter audible from adjoining room (two fresh children's voices)
- Very young boy (little more than three years old, born during preceding winter) somewhere in house crying persistently in dark; mother did not love him, called him "the result of the cold"; when clamor annoying, Thénardier told mother to check boy; mother replied "he bothers me"; child continued shrieking

## Main Characters Status
- **Jean Valjean**: Dead (drowned November 17, 1823, at Toulon)
- **Fantine**: Dead (buried in pauper's grave, January 1823)
- **Cosette**: At Montfermeil with Thénardiers, age approximately 8, serving as household servant
- **Napoleon Bonaparte**: Defeated, imprisoned at Saint Helena

## Themes
- Destiny/chance; divine intervention; human resilience
- Waterloo as historical hinge; war's moral paradox
- Mundane life indifferent to empires; daily tasks continue beneath grand narratives
- Mystery/obscurity: Boulatruelle's search; Valjean's suspicious chain-breaking ease; mill ledger rewritten; sealed letter; letters burned
- Hidden transgressions and buried truths
- Human courage in extremis: Valjean risking life for stranger; topman clinging to rope
- Immense force culminating in immense feebleness affords food for thought
- Poverty and exploitation: Cosette's servitude; water scarcity; Thénardiers' neglect of own child
